A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ECM fungal communities of Douglas fir and paper birch are similar in the oldest two stands of the chronosequence, but are distinct in the younger two stands.
fungal succession is host-specific, with host generalists dominating the ECM communities in the oldest stands, but that fungal succession is not a simple linear process.
ECM fungal community composition stabilized at a relatively early stage of forest succession, while fungal diversity stabilized at a later stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ECM fungal communities of Douglas fir are not similar in composition to those of paper birch, even when the two species co-occur in the same stand.
the ECM fungal community is dynamic and changes over time in a manner that is dependent on host species and site age.
the succession of ECM fungi is not a simple, predictable process, and that it is not driven by a simple, predictable succession of host trees.
